chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Bunan ibn Muhammad, from Musa ibn al-Qasim, from Ali ibn Ja'far, from his brother Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a man who designated his slave girl as a hady (sacrificial offering) for the Ka'bah. How should he deal with it? He said: A man came to my father who had designated his slave girl as a hady for the Ka'bah. So he said to him: 'Evaluate the slave girl or sell her. Then instruct a caller to stand at the Hajar al-Aswad (Black Stone) and call out: 'Indeed, whoever has insufficient funds, or whose path has been cut off, or whose food supply has run out, let him come to so-and-so.' And instruct him to give [the money] to the first one, then the next, until the price of the slave girl is depleted.'

key_terms.الْحِجْر: The Hajar al-Aswad (Black Stone) at the Ka'bah
key_terms.طَرِيقُهُ: His path or journey (often implying travel)
key_terms.قَوِّمِ: Evaluate or appraise the value of
key_terms.لِلْكَعْبَةِ: For the Ka'bah (the sacred house in Mecca)
key_terms.هَدْياً: A sacrificial animal or item dedicated for Hajj or 'Umrah

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a slave dedicated as a sacrifice to the Ka'bah?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi illustrates the Shia juristic principle of 'takhrij al-hady' (extracting the dedication), where a person dedicated to the Ka'bah is freed by selling them and donating the proceeds to the poor. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) specifies that the funds must be distributed to those with specific hardships—limited means, interrupted travel, or exhausted supplies—ensuring the charity reaches the most deserving recipients first. This process transforms a personal vow into a communal welfare act, reflecting the practical application of Quranic charity verses in ritual law.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Bunan Bin Muhammad, from Musa Bin Al Qasim, 
(It has been narrated) from Ali son of Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, from his brother<sup>asws</sup> Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup>, said,

‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about a man made his slave girls as a gift to the Kabah. How should he deal with it?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘A man had come over to my<sup>asws</sup> father, and he had gifted his slave girl to the Kabah. So he<sup>asws</sup> said to him: ‘Evaluate the slave girl, or sell her. Then instruct a caller to stand at the (Black) Stone, so he should call out, ‘Indeed! The one who is short with his expenses, or his way has been cut off (by bandits), or his food supply is exhausted, so let him go to so and so’, and instruct him that he should give first to the first one until the price of the slave girl is depleted’.
en.sarwar: 2. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Bunan ibn Muhammad from Musa ibn al-Qasim from Ali ibn Ja’far who has said the following: “I once asked abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam,

about a man who has made his slave-girl a gift to al- Ka‘bah. What should he do? He (the Imam) said, ‘Once a man who had made his slave-girl a gift to al- Ka‘bah, came to my father, ‘Alayhi al-Salam. He (the Imam) said, ‘Evaluate the slave-girl or sell her; then ask the announcer to stand near the Black Stone and announce, “O those who are short in their expenses, looted on the way or their supplies depleted, come to so and so.” He must distribute it among them on the basis of first come first served until the amount is distributed.’”
